title: Metasurfaces for the nanoscale engineering of light–matter coupling
content:
Nature Reviews Materials, Published online: 05 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41578-026-00951-1

Metasurfaces are optically resonant, open nanophotonic platforms that concentrate and control light at the nanoscale. This Review shows how they provide a common photonic framework across plasmonic, excitonic and phononic material excitations to engineer light–matter coupling, polaritonic states and emergent optical functionalities.

title: From gigawatts to critical mineral demands for EU solar and wind
content:
Nature Energy, Published online: 05 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41560-026-02147-x

Clean energy systems rely on large amounts of minerals. Here the researchers show that meeting EU solar and wind targets will create high demand for copper, zinc, silicon and rare earth elements, especially when offshore wind remains central.

title: A precursor-degassing approach for accessing boron allotropes
content:
Nature Chemistry, Published online: 05 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41557-026-02281-9

The synthesis of a boron allotrope that combines mechanical flexibility and high electrical conductivity is challenging. Now, an open-framework boron allotrope — Imma-B60 — is realized through a precursor-mediated degassing approach. Imma-B60 exhibits a narrow bandgap, high electrical conductivity and plasticity, expanding the potential application of boron beyond superhard and semiconducting phases.

title: The radical-radical cross-coupling of alkyl carboxylic acids and organoborons
content:
Nature Chemistry, Published online: 05 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41557-026-02237-z

Carboxylic acids and boronic acids are abundant feedstocks, yet their direct radical cross-coupling remains challenging due to uncontrolled radical reactivity. Now it has been shown that redox-matched alternating-polarity electrolysis enables their coupling, providing a general platform for C(sp3)–C(sp3) bond formation through synchronized radical generation and controlled radical recombination.
